protections: Path-segment key guard: no segment of a dotted/array path written by set() or transform() may name a prototype-bearing key (__proto__, and arguably constructor/prototype), at ANY position, not only the first. At the pinned commit no such guard exists anywhere (dottie.js:74-107, dottie.js:141-163); package.json:3 is 2.0.3, i.e. before the A fix (2.0.4).

evidence: dottie.js:74 splits the path into pieces with no key filtering
dottie.js:86-89 a non-own segment such as __proto__ is assigned {} (this goes through the __proto__ setter, so the target's prototype is replaced)
dottie.js:94 and dottie.js:107 write the final segment unfiltered, so a last __proto__ segment assigns the caller's value as the prototype
the loop at dottie.js:80-104 treats every index the same way, so a guard on pieces[0] only (the B advisory's 'non-first segment' bypass) leaves indexes 1..n open

traps.reason_to_dismiss: default() only delegates to set(), so a guard inside set() already covers it
evidence: dottie.js:113 calls Dottie.set with the same path; it is closed only if the guard sits inside set() and not in a wrapper
dottie.js:112 get() walks __proto__ first (dottie.js:60) and returns an inherited value, so default() can skip or perform the write depending on what is inherited
dottie.js:142 splits on options.delimiter (set at dottie.js:126), not on '.'
dottie.js:148 uses current.hasOwnProperty(piece), its own copy of the traversal and not set()'s hasOwnProp (dottie.js:86), so a fix in set() does not reach it
dottie.js:149 and dottie.js:153 assign pieces unfiltered at every index; the last-segment write at 153 places object[key] under __proto__
entry points that reach it: Dottie() with one argument (dottie.js:25) and the array branch (dottie.js:119-122); both go through the same loop, so they are the same group

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a key with no delimiter is 'just copied', not a path, so a path-segment guard placed inside the split branch seems complete
evidence: dottie.js:134 Object.keys(object) includes an own '__proto__' key when the input comes from JSON.parse
dottie.js:141 sends delimiter-free keys to the else branch

dottie.js:162 transformed[key] = object[key] with key '__proto__' goes through the setter and replaces transformed's prototype with an object the caller supplies; a guard added only in the loop at dottie.js:146-160 never sees this key

traps.reason_to_dismiss: array paths are documented as arrays of strings; a strict piece === '__proto__' comparison looks complete
evidence: dottie.js:74 uses an array path as-is, with no split and no type normalisation

dottie.js:81 piece may be a non-string element (for example a nested array or an object whose toString gives '__proto__'); property access at dottie.js:86-89 converts it to the string '__proto__', while a strict === string check does not
test/set.test.js:52 shows that array paths keep dot-containing segments whole, so the guard must compare per element after String() conversion, not on a joined or re-split string

conflicts.what: A T1 fix that joins an array path and re-splits it on '.' (or one regex over the joined string) breaks the must-keep-working array path with dot-containing segments (test/set.test.js:51-54, dottie.js:74).

Rejecting every key that contains '__proto__' as a substring, or throwing on the whole object in transform, also refuses legitimate keys like 'a.__proto__x' or 'proto_field', and changes the null-break behaviour at dottie.js:157-159 (test/transform.test.js:89-102) if the guard is placed after the break.

fairness_risks: Whether 'constructor' and 'prototype' must be refused is not set by the pinned code. Neither is a prototype route through set()/transform() here, because set's hasOwnProp check (dottie.js:86-89) and transform's (dottie.js:148-149) replace a non-own 'constructor' with a fresh {}. Hidden tests that require refusing them would penalise a correct __proto__-only fix, and tests that require them to keep working would penalise a broad blocklist.

Silent skip, throw, or no-op is unspecified for a refused segment. set() already throws for unsuitable targets (dottie.js:77, dottie.js:98), while transform never throws. Tests should check the outcome (no prototype change on the target, Object.prototype clean), not the error mode.
Custom delimiters (dottie.js:126, dottie.js:142, test/transform.test.js:123-147) must keep working; a guard hard-coded to split on '.' is wrong for delimiter '_'.
Array paths with dot-containing segments must keep working (test/set.test.js:51-54).
force:true overwrite of null and non-object values must keep working (test/set.test.js:42-49, test/set.test.js:62-67; dottie.js:88).

design.why: Of the three independent fix sites in dottie.js, set() (T1, with T5 as a shape of the same guard), the delimited transform loop (T3) and the transform plain-key branch (T4), this design uses all three, plus T5 as the how-type judgement inside set's guard. T4 is the deepseek-type trap: the protection is absent, and the reason to dismiss it is strong ('not a path'). T5 is the mimo-type trap: a how-type key-coercion shape where strict comparison or an over-broad join/regex either misses it or breaks array paths. T1 and T3 are the advisory routes the report points at, so they anchor the task. Weakness: there are only 3 truly independent groups, all in one 228-line file at distance 0, and T5 shares T1's fix site, so the stack is at the lower bound of 3. T2 adds no independent judgement and is left out.

unverified: The contents of the A fix 7d3aee1c9c3c and the B fix 7e8fa1345a4b. The pinned tree (package.json:3, version 2.0.3) predates both, so whether A guarded only pieces[0] (as the B summary implies), and therefore a_fix_leaves_b_open and b_in_code_a_wrote, cannot be checked from the pinned code.

Whether a global Object.prototype write is reachable at the pinned code. From reading dottie.js:86-89 and dottie.js:148-149, a non-own '__proto__' segment is assigned a fresh {} through the __proto__ setter, which replaces the target object's own prototype rather than writing to Object.prototype. Not executed; hidden tests should assert both Object.getPrototypeOf(target) === Object.prototype and a clean ({}).polluted.
The T5 coercion route assumes callers can pass non-string array path elements (for example from parsed JSON). Not shown in this repo.
Whether the upstream B fix also covers the transform non-delimited branch (T4) or get() traversal (dottie.js:60).
